name: URL Encoder / Decoder
description: Percent-encode or decode text for safe use in URLs and query strings, with both strict component and form-field (+ for space) modes.

faq.question: What's the difference between "Component" and "Form field" mode?
faq.answer: Component mode uses strict percent-encoding (encodeURIComponent), where a space becomes %20 — correct for a single value you're inserting into a URL path or query string by hand. Form field mode additionally turns spaces into + instead of %20, matching how browsers encode application/x-www-form-urlencoded form submissions and query strings you copy from an address bar. Decoding the wrong mode against the wrong kind of string is a common source of literal + characters showing up where a space should be.

faq.question: Why would decoding fail?
faq.answer: Percent-encoded text must use exactly two hex digits after every %. A stray % (from text that was never actually encoded, or was double-encoded incorrectly) will fail to decode — the error message points at that being the likely cause.
